description: The curated baseline of the Passport wallet matrix: one row per wallet, connection path and family, one cell per capability, each with a value, a reason and evidence. Research read on 2026-10-25; workspace tests from 2026-09-04 to 2026-10-23.

families.label: EVM
families.format: EIP-712 V1 typed data through eth_signTypedData_v4: domain {name 'Midnight Passport', version '1', verifyingContract}, no chainId. personal_sign signs only the blind request.

families.label: Solana
families.format: solana:signMessage over the arm's 50-byte raw head and the text, or off-chain message v1 (solana:signOffchainMessage where the wallet offers it). Hardware signs off-chain messages only.

families.label: Cardano
families.format: CIP-30 signData through the reward address: CIP-8 COSE_Sign1, payload unhashed, header layout 1 (a fixed 32-byte prefix and the text) or layout 2 (Lace, the text).

capabilities.label: Connects
capabilities.description: The page reaches the wallet for this family: through the family's discovery standard (EIP-6963, Wallet Standard, the NEAR wallet selector, CIP-30), or, for a direct hardware row, through Ledger's device SDK or Trezor Connect.

capabilities.label: Signs the arm's format
capabilities.description: The wallet signs the bytes the family's arm verifies (see the family's format).

capabilities.label: Shows readable text
capabilities.description: Before signing, the wallet shows the approval text or typed-data fields readably, not as hex, hashes or a bare summary. A valid signature says nothing about this.

capabilities.label: Deterministic (can hold a blind)
capabilities.description: Signing the same bytes twice gives the same signature, so the blind derived from a signature can be restored.

capabilities.label: Completes the operations on chain
capabilities.description: The Passport operations complete on a chain with this wallet. Only the local-stack runs and the stagenet session measure it.

values.label: Check
values.description: Shown to hold for this row: by a test or emulator run in this workspace, or by a primary source stating the capability.

values.label: Warning
values.description: Holds with a caveat the reason states: a setting, a limit, a display problem, or one condition the arm needs that a source leaves unconfirmed.

values.label: Cross
values.description: Shown not to hold, by a test or a primary source.

values.label: Not yet measured
values.description: Nothing decides it yet. Not the same as unsupported.

states.description: This workspace's own wallet sessions or emulator runs back the row.

evidence.title: MetaMask: Passport EIP-712 session
evidence.description: The owner signed Passport approvals (rotate_enc_key, issue_grant) with MetaMask in this workspace's signing lab. EIP-712 V1 typed data (domain without chainId) and personal_sign text verified offline. A V2 request carrying a chainId was refused because it did not match the wallet's active network. MetaMask showed labelled fields, the user's own account and the effect text, and also its active network (Sepolia), although nothing signed names a chain. personal_sign text was shown whole, with its line breaks. Each digest was signed once.

evidence.title: Backpack (EVM): Passport EIP-712 session
evidence.description: The owner signed rotate_enc_key typed data with Backpack's EVM provider. V0, V1 and V2 were all signed, with no chain check; the V1 signature verified offline. Backpack showed raw JSON: the message and the whole domain. Each digest was signed once.

evidence.title: Rabby: Passport EIP-712 session
evidence.description: The owner signed rotate_enc_key with Rabby through EIP-6963 and through window.ethereum. V1 typed data and personal_sign text verified offline; V2 was refused ('chainId should be same as current chainId'). The same V1 digest signed through the two entries gave identical signatures. Rabby labelled the request 'Unknown Signature Type', showed raw JSON and 'Chain: Ethereum'.

surface.network: Ethereum mainnet selected; nothing was sent on chain

evidence.title: Coinbase Wallet: Passport EIP-712 session
evidence.description: The owner signed rotate_enc_key with the Coinbase Wallet extension. V1 and personal_sign verified offline; V2 was signed too, with no chain check. Every signature recovered to the connected account, so the account was a key account, not a smart account. What the wallet displayed was not recorded. Each digest was signed once.

evidence.title: EVM arm: real-wallet signatures through the circuits
evidence.description: After the EVM arm was refactored to the fixed EIP-712 V1 domain, its verifying circuits accepted the six real-wallet V1 signatures of 2026-10-21 (MetaMask twice, Rabby twice, Coinbase Wallet, Backpack) and a local proof server proved them. The same wallets' V0 and V2 signatures were refused. The arm's pure circuits also verified the 35 emulator V1 signatures and refused 140 V0, V2 and personal_sign negatives.

surface.access: offline circuits and a local proof server

evidence.title: MetaMask and Phantom (EVM): determinism spike
evidence.description: A spike page in this workspace asked for one EIP-712 message, whose domain has no chainId, repeatedly and from several wallets holding the same key: MetaMask, Phantom's EVM provider and a software wallet. The signatures were byte-identical. The message was a test message, not a Passport approval.

evidence.title: Phantom (Solana): Passport message sessions
evidence.description: On 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21 the owner signed Passport approval texts (491 and 1,690 bytes) with Phantom, through its injected provider and its Wallet Standard entry. Raw messages verified offline, and five signatures of the same bytes over two sessions were identical. Every off-chain message v1 request was refused ('You cannot sign solana transactions using sign message'). The text was shown with its line breaks.

surface.access: Wallet Standard and the injected provider (window.phantom.solana)

evidence.title: Backpack (Solana): Passport message sessions
evidence.description: On 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21 the owner signed rotate_enc_key with Backpack through Wallet Standard. Raw messages verified, and so did the off-chain message v1 envelope (541 bytes), both when the page built it and when Backpack built it through its own solana:signOffchainMessage. Four off-chain signatures over two sessions were identical. Backpack decoded the envelope and showed only the text, with its line breaks. It offers 'Auto-approve message signing' for 24 hours. With Phantom also installed, Backpack answered three requests made through Phantom's Wallet Standard entry with its own key; the signer check caught all three.

evidence.title: Solflare: Passport message session
evidence.description: The owner signed rotate_enc_key with Solflare through Wallet Standard. Raw messages verified, and so did off-chain message v1 through Solflare's own signOffchainMessage (541 bytes, the same envelope Ledger, Trezor and Backpack sign). Repeated signatures were identical (one session). Raw text and Solflare's own off-chain text were shown cleanly; a page-built envelope passed as a raw message was signed but shown with its prefix as garbled characters.

evidence.title: Solana arm: real-wallet signatures after the refactor
evidence.description: The refactored Solana arm accepts a raw message (a fixed 50-byte head and the text) or an off-chain message v1. The real-wallet off-chain signatures (Backpack, Solflare) verify on its off-chain path and fail on the raw path. The real-wallet raw signatures predate the head, so the same texts were re-signed with software test keys until the owner re-signs with the wallets. The three Backpack answers to Phantom requests are refused before proving.

evidence.title: Meteor: NEP-413 session
evidence.description: The owner signed Passport texts with Meteor on NEAR testnet through the wallet selector's Meteor adapter and through Meteor's own SDK. NEP-413 verified offline for add_device, issue_grant (1,690 bytes) and the blind request; repeated signatures were identical in one session. Through the selector callbackUrl is absent. Meteor's SDK keeps a callbackUrl and signs it without showing it, which gives a different blind for the same text. Meteor showed the site, the account and the message, with the full text behind 'View Full Message'; line breaks were collapsed, and the recipient and nonce were not shown. It framed the request as one that does not execute anything on the blockchain.

evidence.title: MyNearWallet: adapter run with a simulated wallet
evidence.description: The signing lab ran the wallet selector's MyNearWallet adapter against a simulated wallet response. No real MyNearWallet signature exists: the owner's session skipped it because the wallet sunsets on 2026-10-31.

evidence.title: Eternl: CIP-30 signData session
evidence.description: The owner signed Passport texts with Eternl on Cardano preprod. Every signature verified offline: header layout 1, payload unhashed (up to 1,690 bytes). Through the reward address Eternl signs with the stake key. Repeated requests gave identical signatures, and the stake-key blind was reproduced over three signatures and two sessions, across a browser restart. Eternl shows the full text in a scroll box but collapses line breaks and padding, and frames the request as 'Confirm you own the requested key'.

evidence.title: Lace: CIP-30 signData session
evidence.description: The owner signed issue_grant (1,690 bytes) with Lace through the reward address and through a change address: header layout 2, payload unhashed, both verified offline. The session's first requests failed with APIError -4 (AccountChange) before signing succeeded. One signature per address, so determinism was not measured; what Lace displayed was not recorded.

evidence.title: Ledger Ethereum app 1.22.5 on Speculos
evidence.description: Eleven of the EVM arm's frozen EIP-712 vectors and the personal_sign blind request, on a Ledger Flex (Nano S Plus subset). By default the app refuses the arm's V1 typed data with 0x6a80 ('cannot be clear-signed'). With blind signing enabled it shows a loss-of-funds warning, then the fields, readable except one 192-byte value cut after 187 bytes; the hashed path shows only two hashes. personal_sign works with default settings: first lines, then 'More' shows the whole text (the Nano S Plus turns line breaks into spaces). Every signature recovers to the test seed's address, and every repeat is identical.

evidence.title: Trezor Safe 5: EIP-712 and personal_sign
evidence.description: The EVM arm's V1 typed data is shown readably: every field as name (type) and value, whole (issue_grant: 29 fields over 46 screens). The review can be skipped by confirming the 'Contains N keys' summary. personal_sign text is shown whole over four pages, with no warning. Every signature recovers to the test seed's address, every repeat is identical, and the blind is reproduced.

evidence.title: Trezor Safe 5: Solana off-chain messages
evidence.description: The device signs Passport texts as off-chain message v1 (the same bytes as the Ledger Solana app), never as raw bytes. By default the screen shows only the first lines and offers 'Confirm without review'; the full text is in a menu. Signatures are deterministic.

surface.emulator: trezor-user-env, Trezor Safe 5 emulator, public test seed

evidence.title: Trezor Safe 5: Cardano CIP-8
evidence.description: CIP-8 with header layout 1, never hashed: every approval (369 to 1,690 bytes) and probes up to 32,768 bytes, verified and deterministic. Any payload containing a line feed or padding is shown as hex (18 characters a line, 7 to 29 pages for the approvals); single-line ASCII is shown as text. The address and the network are never shown, and the device does not check that the header address belongs to the signing key. Stake-key and payment-key blinds were identical over four signatures and three sessions, across an emulator restart.
